thread:
Aisha (People Ops): thanks everyone who hopped on the all-hands Q&A — recording and notes are up, leaving the highlights and a few follow-ups here so folks who missed it can catch up. TL;DR: review cycle dates, calibration window, promotion eligibility criteria, and comp band changes.
Tom R (Eng): could you confirm the effective date for promotions+raises? the all-hands slide was a bit fuzzy.
Aisha (People Ops): good call — promotions will be effective the first of the month after final approvals. so if approvals finish by May 20, effective date is June 1. comp increases start the same date.
Denise (Eng): what counts as "final approvals"? is that manager sign-off + calibration or exec sign-off?
Aisha (People Ops): manager sign-off + committee calibration are required. exec sign-off only for exceptions (late promotions or level skips). calibration window closes at 11:59pm PT on the date in the schedule.
Marco (ML): i missed the initial calibration email — is there still a way to get onto the agenda if my manager already submitted a case?
Aisha (People Ops): yes — ask your manager to submit an "add to calibration" note via the form by EOD Wed. we triage a small late queue (why we prefer earlier submissions tho).
PeopleOps Bot: Reminder: Calibration form due in 48h — https://confluence.redwood/people/calibration-form :bell:
Ben K (Manager): regarding raises, are promotions automatically matched to midpoint of new band or is there a policy? we have a case where market comp is above band.
Aisha (People Ops): we aim to move people at least to the new minimum for the level. midpoint adjustments happen case-by-case during comp committee. if market comp > band, we escalate to compensation team for an exception review — expect ~2 weeks processing for exceptions.
Tom R (Eng): is there retro pay for promotions that land after a delay (e.g., approval late but effective date pushed)?
Aisha (People Ops): retro pay is only for approvals where paperwork is delayed on our side — if the committee approves with an earlier effective date, payroll will process retro pay. manager-requested delays do not get retro.
Denise (Eng): has the leveling rubric been updated? i remember a draft. link?
Aisha (People Ops): yes — new rubric v2 is live. see: https://redwood.company/people/leveling (internal) — highlights: clearer scope examples for L3->L4, added "impact over time" evidence, and updated examples for senior IC vs manager paths.
Denise (Eng): thanks — will share with team. also, what's the appeals path if someone thinks criteria were misapplied?
Aisha (People Ops): appeals go to People Ops + review panel. steps: 1) manager and IC discuss and document missing context; 2) submit appeals form (link above) within 10 business days of outcome; 3) review panel meets within 7 business days. appeals are for process errors or missed evidence, not re-running calibration.
Marco (ML): quick practical Q — what fields are required on the calibration form? helps managers prepare.
Aisha (People Ops): minimal required fields:
```
- employee_name
- current_level
- proposed_level
- summary_of_evidence (3 bullets)
- manager_recommendation
- compensation_request (if any)
```
Aisha (People Ops): please keep bullets short. attach supporting docs if helpful.
Ben K (Manager): appreciate the clarity. will sync with my managers. :thumbsup:
Tom R (Eng): thanks Aisha — this cleared up several items.
Aisha (People Ops): great! i'll post a consolidated FAQ + timeline in #announcements by end of day and leave this thread open for any follow-ups. ping me or DM if you need a 1:1 for specific cases. :slightly_smiling_face:
